overview: This PR extends native structured output support so that any StructuredOutputConverter (not only BeanOutputConverter) can provide a JSON Schema to be used by the ChatClient when native structured output is enabled.

changes.description: Adds a default getJsonSchema() contract and a sentinel constant for “no schema”.
Marks getJsonSchema() with @Override to match the new interface method.
Uses StructuredOutputConverter#getJsonSchema() when native structured output is enabled.
Adds tests to verify custom converters participate in native structured output and schema propagation.

issues.content: When native structured output is enabled, this unconditionally overwrites any existing STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA context entry with outputConverter.getJsonSchema(). Since StructuredOutputConverter#getJsonSchema() now defaults to an empty string, this can clobber a user-provided schema that was set explicitly via request.context(...), effectively disabling native structured output unintentionally.

Same issue as above in the entity(...) path: when native structured output is enabled, the code overwrites any pre-existing STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA context value with outputConverter.getJsonSchema(), even when that is blank (the new default). This can accidentally erase a schema that was set directly on the request context.

JsonMapper#readTree(String) throws a checked Jackson exception; StructuredOutputConverter#convert cannot declare checked exceptions, so this implementation won't compile as-is. Wrap the parse call in a try/catch and rethrow as an unchecked exception (consistent with other JSON parsing helpers in the codebase).

overview: This PR updates the Spring AI Mistral integration to align Jackson (de)serialization with Mistral’s OpenAPI-defined chat message content shapes (string vs structured chunks), and adds support for reasoning-model features such as reasoning_effort plus emitting reference/thinking metadata from responses.

changes.description: Adds a references payload fixture used by citations/reference integration tests.
Adds fixture for message content as plain string.
Adds fixture for message content represented as typed chunks (including thinking).
Adds fixture for standalone content chunks serialization/deserialization tests.
Adds test utilities for reasoning (“thinking”) models and reasoning effort defaults.
Adds a JUnit @EnumSource meta-annotation for reasoning model parameterized tests.
Refactors retry tests to new finish-reason enum and updated response/result access.
Extends options tests to cover reasoningEffort.
Adds IT coverage for reference metadata + thinking-model call/stream behavior.
Updates request mapping tests to assert chunk-based user content instead of legacy media content.
Adjusts tool-calling IT assertions to use extracted text content and minor refactors.
Updates tool-calling IT to use extracted text content and refactors fields/formatting.
Adds comprehensive unit tests for chunk content serialization/deserialization and extraction helpers.
Expands API IT coverage for chunk content, references, and thinking-model behavior (call + stream).
Updates runtime hints tests to reflect finish reason enum rename and matching logic.
Adds reasoningEffort option, wires it through builder/mutation/equality logic.
Adds reference/thinking metadata extraction; maps chunk content to assistant text output; adds request parameter wiring for reasoning_effort.
Updates finish reason enum usage and adapts merge logic to content being non-string.
Implements chunk-based content mapping, adds reasoning_effort, introduces shared FinishReason, and refines Javadoc/typing.
Adjusts test dependencies (adds explicit jsonassert).

issues.content: mock() is called without providing the class to mock. Mockito/BDDMockito requires mock(SomeClass.class) here, otherwise this test won't compile.

hashCode() is inconsistent with equals(): it omits toolNames (which is compared in equals) and includes this.tools twice. This breaks the equals/hashCode contract and can cause incorrect behavior in hash-based collections.

Tool responses are sent back to the model using tool_call_id. Allowing a null toolResponse.id() here can produce an invalid request (and other parts of the codebase assume tool response ids are always non-null). Consider restoring the invariant check before constructing the TOOL message.
Typo in deprecation comment: "planed" -> "planned".
Typo in Javadoc: "suing" -> "using".

overview: Adds a new S3-backed ChatMemoryRepository implementation to persist conversations as JSON objects in S3 (and S3-compatible stores), along with Spring Boot auto-configuration, a starter, BOM/module wiring, and documentation.

changes.description: New starter for the S3 chat memory repository.
Adds S3 repository docs, configuration properties, and examples.
Adds BOM entries for S3 modules and adjusts chat-memory auto-config entries.
Registers new S3 repository + auto-config + starter modules in the build.
Integration tests for S3 repository via LocalStack.
Core S3-backed repository implementation (CRUD + listing + JSON serialization).
Builder-based configuration + validation for S3 repository.
Nullness annotation/package docs for the S3 repository package.
Module README with setup, usage, and operational guidance.
New S3 repository module POM and dependencies (AWS SDK v2 S3, Jackson, tests).
Integration tests for Spring Boot auto-configuration.
Registers S3 auto-configuration.
Spring Boot configuration properties for S3 chat memory.
Auto-configures S3Client and S3ChatMemoryRepository.
Nullness annotation/package docs for the S3 auto-config package.
New S3 auto-config module POM and dependencies.

issues.content: This auto-configuration should run *before* ChatMemoryAutoConfiguration; otherwise Boot may create the default InMemoryChatMemoryRepository first, and this S3 repository bean will never be created due to @ConditionalOnMissingBean conditions. Other chat-memory repository auto-configs in this repo declare @AutoConfiguration(before = ChatMemoryAutoConfiguration.class) for this reason.

@ConditionalOnMissingBean({ S3ChatMemoryRepository.class, ChatMemory.class, ChatMemoryRepository.class }) is too broad: if an application defines its own ChatMemory bean (common when customizing window size) this auto-config will skip creating the S3 repository even though it's still needed. Repository auto-configs elsewhere in this repo typically only guard on the repository type.

The auto-config reads the custom S3 endpoint from System.getProperty("spring.ai.chat.memory.repository.s3.endpoint"). This bypasses Spring Boot’s normal configuration binding (e.g., application.properties, env vars) and makes the feature harder to discover/operate. Consider adding an endpoint (and possibly path-style-access) field to S3ChatMemoryProperties and reading it from properties instead.

The BOM now references spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-chat-memory-repository-redis, but that artifact/module does not exist in this repo (the existing Redis auto-config module is spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-chat-memory-redis). This will break dependency management for consumers relying on the BOM entry.

Importing org.testcontainers.localstack.LocalStackContainer is inconsistent with the rest of the repo (which uses org.testcontainers.containers.localstack.LocalStackContainer) and is likely to fail to compile on the Testcontainers version pulled in by Spring Boot.

Using localstack/localstack:latest and withServices("s3") makes these integration tests non-deterministic and may not compile/run with the LocalStackContainer API (which typically expects LocalStackContainer.Service enums). Elsewhere in the repo, LocalStack is pinned to a specific version.

LocalStackContainer typically exposes the S3 endpoint via getEndpointOverride(Service.S3) rather than getEndpoint(). With the correct LocalStackContainer import, getEndpoint() is likely missing, causing compilation errors.

This test imports org.testcontainers.localstack.LocalStackContainer, which is inconsistent with the org.testcontainers.containers.localstack.LocalStackContainer used elsewhere in the repo and is likely to fail compilation with the Testcontainers version managed by Spring Boot.

Using localstack/localstack:latest plus withServices("s3") makes tests flaky and may not match the LocalStackContainer API (typically expects LocalStackContainer.Service enums). Pinning the LocalStack image version is more stable (the repo already pins LocalStack elsewhere).
With the correct LocalStackContainer type, the endpoint is typically retrieved via getEndpointOverride(Service.S3) rather than getEndpoint(). Using getEndpoint() is likely to fail compilation.

keyPrefix can be explicitly set to an empty/blank value, which later breaks listing and key generation (e.g., findConversationIds() will list under "/", and default key generation asserts prefix has text). It’s better to treat blank as “use default” (or fail fast) during config construction.

initializeBucket uses createBucket(CreateBucketRequest.builder().bucket(...).build()) with no region/location constraint. On AWS, bucket creation outside us-east-1 typically requires a CreateBucketConfiguration with the correct location constraint, otherwise bucket creation fails. Since S3ChatMemoryProperties supports configurable region, bucket auto-initialization should take that into account (or document the limitation).

The README claims “The repository includes comprehensive property-based tests using jqwik”, but there are no jqwik tests/dependency in this module. This is misleading documentation; either add jqwik-based tests or reword this section as an example.

The LocalStack example uses localstack/localstack:latest and .withServices("s3"), which is brittle and may not match current Testcontainers APIs. Consider pinning the image version (as elsewhere in the repo) and using LocalStackContainer.Service.S3.

The LocalStack example uses localstack.getEndpoint(); with org.testcontainers.containers.localstack.LocalStackContainer the usual API is getEndpointOverride(LocalStackContainer.Service.S3). Updating the snippet avoids copy/paste compile failures for users.

overview: This PR introduces a new Spring AI VectorStore implementation backed by Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (via the Bedrock Agent Runtime Retrieve API), along with Spring Boot auto-configuration, a starter, and documentation to enable similarity search and metadata filtering against pre-configured Knowledge Bases.

changes.description: Core Bedrock KB-backed VectorStore implementation (search, pagination, metadata mapping).
Converts Spring AI portable filter AST to Bedrock RetrievalFilter.
Package nullness annotation and package doc.
Unit tests for builder validation, similarity search mapping, pagination behavior, etc.
Integration tests against a real KB (env-gated).
Unit tests for filter conversion (comparisons, lists, logical ops, value types).
New module POM and dependencies (AWS Bedrock Agent Runtime).
Auto-configures Bedrock client + vector store from properties.
Boot configuration properties for Bedrock KB vector store.
Package nullness annotation and package doc.
Registers the auto-configuration.
New auto-config module POM.
New Spring Boot starter POM.
Registers new vector store type id (bedrock-knowledge-base).
Adds new modules (store/autoconfig/starter) to BOM dependency management.
Adds new modules to the multi-module build.
New user documentation page for Bedrock KB vector store.
Adds the Bedrock KB page to the docs navigation.

issues.content: defaultTopK / defaultSimilarityThreshold configured on the VectorStore (including via Boot properties) are effectively ignored for the common VectorStoreRetriever#similaritySearch(String) path, because the interface default builds a SearchRequest with its own defaults (topK=4, similarityThreshold=0.0) and this method then prefers the request values. Align with other VectorStore implementations (e.g., Azure) by overriding similaritySearch(String) to apply the store defaults, and simplify the threshold calculation (the current >= 0 fallback is dead code since SearchRequest never allows negative thresholds).

Pagination currently requests numberOfResults(topK) on every page. On subsequent pages this can over-fetch (and potentially increase latency/cost) even when only a few more results are needed to reach the requested topK. Consider requesting only the remaining number of results for each subsequent call.

The class-level enablement condition requires AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, but the Javadoc says credentials may be provided via the default AWS credential chain (profiles, web identity, instance role, etc.). Requiring AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID prevents these integration tests from running in common CI setups that rely on role-based credentials. Consider gating only on BEDROCK_KB_ID and letting the SDK's default provider chain decide whether credentials are available.

Filter.ExpressionType includes ISNULL / ISNOTNULL, and the text parser/DSL can produce these. Right now the converter falls into the default case and throws UnsupportedOperationException, which will break metadata filtering for expressions like field IS NULL / field IS NOT NULL. Consider mapping these to Bedrock filters (e.g., equals/notEquals with a null value) instead of throwing.

overview: This PR focuses on improving performance and reducing allocations in Spring AI’s model/tool infrastructure, mainly by optimizing repeated lookups during tool resolution and bean merging.

changes.description: Replaces per-tool linear search with precomputed Set membership checks when merging tool callbacks and tool names.
Optimizes interface method name membership checks via Set, and refactors getter-name construction to reduce allocations.

issues.content: chatOptions.getToolCallbacks() is called twice; since you already copied it into toolCallbacks, you can build existingToolNames from that local list to avoid any potential recomputation and keep the method consistent with the stated allocation/perf goals.

The PR description mentions removing substring usage and improving null-safety here, but the implementation still calls name.substring(1) and still throws on null/empty input. Either update the PR description to match the behavior, or harden/adjust this helper to actually meet those goals.

overview: This PR updates the MCP Server Boot Starter documentation to explain how to propagate transport-specific metadata (notably HTTP headers) into MCP tools via McpTransportContext, with new code examples and minor formatting cleanup.

changes.description: Added a new “Adding data to McpTransportContext” section describing TransportContextExtractor usage and how to read transport context from McpSyncRequestContext/McpAsyncRequestContext.
Introduced practical Java snippets showing how to extract the Authorization header and access it inside an @McpTool.
Cleaned up minor whitespace/formatting issues in the existing documentation.

issues.content: The code sample for contextExtractor will throw at runtime when the Authorization header is missing because Map.of(...) does not allow null values. Also, the ObjectMapper parameter is currently unused, and defining this bean will override the starter’s @ConditionalOnMissingBean auto-configuration, so the example should show the core builder setup (json mapper + streamable-http properties) to remain functional when copy/pasted.
Minor grammar: in “(for example, HTTP headers, remote host, etc)”, the period belongs with “etc.” (or rewrite to avoid the parenthetical punctuation).

overview: This PR addresses an MCP Gateway proxying issue where tool call results were being double-wrapped into TextContent, losing richer MCP content structure. It introduces parsing logic to detect and preserve serialized MCP List results so gateway/proxy scenarios return structured content (text/image/audio/resource links) instead of a JSON string blob.

changes.description: Introduces parseContentList() and routes sync tool results through it to avoid double-wrapping and preserve MCP content structure.
Adds integration-style tests for proxied serialized content handling through toSyncToolSpecification().
Adds direct unit tests for parseContentList() across content shapes and fallback scenarios.

issues.content: parseContentList() currently treats *any* non-empty JSON array as an MCP content list. If a normal tool returns a JSON array that isn’t MCP content (e.g., a list of domain objects), this else branch will split the array into multiple TextContent entries (and log a warning per element), changing the previous behavior where the whole string was returned as a single TextContent. For backward compatibility, when an array element doesn’t match a recognized MCP content shape, the method should fall back to wrapping the original callResult as a single TextContent (not one per element).

In the {data, mimeType} branch, textValue() can return null (e.g., if mimeType is null in the JSON or non-text), which will currently trigger an NPE at mimeType.startsWith(...). Also, any non-audio mimeType is treated as an ImageContent, which misclassifies non-image binary types (e.g., application/pdf). Consider using path(...).asText(null) with null checks, and only mapping to ImageContent when mimeType starts with image (otherwise fall back to wrapping the original callResult).

parseContentList() is intended to preserve backward compatibility for non-MCP tool results. There’s currently no test ensuring that a *non-empty* JSON array that is not an MCP Content list (e.g., an array of objects without MCP fields) is wrapped as a single TextContent rather than being split into multiple content entries. Adding such a regression test will help prevent future accidental behavior changes.

overview: This PR adds OpenAI Java SDK–based text-to-speech (audio speech) support to the Spring AI OpenAI SDK module, including model/options types, response metadata (rate-limits), and Spring Boot auto-configuration with accompanying tests.

changes.description: New TTS model implementation backed by the OpenAI Java SDK.
New options type for configuring model/voice/format/speed and connection settings.
Extracts rate-limit metadata from OpenAI SDK HTTP response headers.
New RateLimit implementation used by the audio-speech metadata.
Unit tests for model construction/defaults/options behavior.
Unit tests for rate-limit header extraction into response metadata.
Integration tests against the live API (guarded by OPENAI_API_KEY).
Adds Boot auto-configuration wiring for the new audio speech model.
Adds Boot properties binding for audio speech defaults and options.
Registers the new auto-configuration class.
Integration test validating the auto-configuration and property binding.

issues.content: When the SDK returns an empty response body, the code returns a TextToSpeechResponse without attaching response metadata. This drops potentially useful headers (e.g., rate-limit data) and makes the response shape inconsistent (metadata sometimes present, sometimes absent).

Builder.from(...) sets the model twice (once under “Parent class fields” and again under “Child class fields”). The second assignment is redundant and makes it harder to reason about what is actually considered a parent vs child option.

RateLimit’s getters are contractually non-null (see spring-ai-model/.../RateLimit), but this implementation stores nullable fields and returns them directly. That can propagate nulls to callers and cause NPEs, and it diverges from existing RateLimit implementations (e.g., OpenAiRateLimit / EmptyRateLimit) which always return non-null values. Consider normalizing missing/invalid headers to 0L / Duration.ZERO so the RateLimit contract is upheld; tests expecting nulls should be adjusted accordingly.

This constructs OpenAiSdkRateLimit with potentially null values (remaining/reset may be missing/invalid while limit is present). Since RateLimit’s getters are non-null by contract, consider normalizing any missing/invalid numeric/duration headers to 0L / Duration.ZERO before constructing the RateLimit (or otherwise ensuring the resulting RateLimit never returns null).

overview: This PR addresses GH-4545 by hardening filter-expression serialization against injection via unescaped string literals across multiple vector-store filter converters. It introduces centralized/default escaping in AbstractFilterExpressionConverter (JSON-style) and store-specific escaping for SQL (MariaDB), OData (Azure AI Search), SpEL (SimpleVectorStore), and Weaviate’s filter format, plus dedicated security regression tests in each module.

changes.description: Adds default string escaping hook and applies it in doSingleValue() for JSON-like converters.
Adds regression tests for escaping behavior inherited by JSON-like converters (via Pinecone).
Escapes SpEL string literals to prevent quote-based expression injection.
Adds SpEL-focused escaping/injection regression tests.
Escapes valueText / valueDate values in Weaviate filter output.
Adds Weaviate-specific escaping/injection regression tests.
Escapes SQL string literals to mitigate injection in MariaDB filter output.
Adds SQL escaping/injection regression tests for MariaDB.
Escapes OData string literals (single-quote doubling) to mitigate injection.
Adds OData escaping/injection regression tests for Azure AI Search.

issues.content: escapeStringValue currently escapes backslashes and double-quotes, but it does not escape JSON control characters (e.g., \n, \r, \t). If a filter value contains a literal newline/tab, the generated Pinecone/JSON-style filter becomes invalid JSON and can still break the filter syntax. Escaping these control characters keeps the output valid and makes the "Control characters" security tests meaningful.

This test is named "Control characters should be escaped" but it only asserts that the plain text fragments are present. It never verifies that newline/tab characters are actually escaped (e.g., as \\n and \\t), so it would pass even if the output contains literal control characters and invalid JSON.

The assertion in this test is too broad: contains("\\") will pass as long as the output contains any backslash, even if double-quotes or backslashes are not escaped correctly. Making the assertions specific helps ensure this test actually detects regressions in escaping behavior.

doesNotMatch("path:\\[.*path:\\[") uses .* which does not match newlines by default. The Weaviate filter output includes newlines, so this assertion can miss cases where multiple path:[ segments appear on different lines (i.e., a false negative). Enabling DOTALL makes the regex robust.

overview: This PR is an incremental step toward the broader ChatOptions “options rework” (#5441) by introducing a more type-safe, consistently-typed builder API (self-referential generics), adding mutate()/combineWith(...) hooks, and establishing a reusable test base for validating builder behavior across implementations.

changes.description: New reusable test base to validate builder instance creation and mutate() behavior.
Builder API updated to generic self-typing and more precise return types.
Adds a builder mixin interface for structured output schema configuration.
Reworks builder to extend shared base builder, adds mutate(), combineWith(...), and new build semantics.
Refactors default builder into a generic, self-typed builder with combineWith(...).
Adds mutate(), updates copy() to builder-based copying, and implements equals/hashCode.
Introduces generic builder type, adds mutate() contract, and defines combineWith(...).
Updates tests to use the shared abstract test base; adjusts numeric assertions for float fields.
Migrates Ollama options to the new builder approach, adds mutate(), and reworks toMap().
Adds spring-ai-test as a test dependency to support the new shared test base.

issues.content: toolNames(Set) assigns the provided Set directly to the builder field. If callers pass an immutable set (e.g., Set.of(...)) and later call toolNames(String...), the subsequent addAll(...) will throw UnsupportedOperationException. Copying into a mutable HashSet avoids this and also prevents unexpected external mutation of the builder state.

combineWith(...) copies toolCallbacks and toolNames by reference (this.toolCallbacks = options.toolCallbacks, etc.). Because the builder mutates these collections in-place (e.g., toolCallbacks(...)/toolNames(...) add to the existing collections), the two builders can end up sharing state: mutating either builder after combineWith can unexpectedly change the other. Copy the collections instead to keep builders independent.

OllamaChatOptions.Builder#build() passes the builder's mutable collections (toolCallbacks, toolNames, toolContext) straight into the constructed options without copying. Since OllamaChatOptions exposes these collections directly via getters, the built options can end up sharing mutable state with the builder (and with other options built from the same builder). This can cause changes made after build() (e.g., adding a tool name on the builder) to retroactively affect already-built options. Copy the collections (and stopSequences) when constructing the options instance.
